acronymStudy.meaning: Names the original 5 Gb/s SuperSpeed USB specification.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Three-point-zero introduced the five-gigabit lane.
acronymStudy.distinction: This historical speed tier was later renamed USB 3.1 Gen 1 and USB 3.2 Gen 1.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a USB specification revision associated with Gen 1 and Gen 2 speed labels.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Three-point-one requires checking which Generation is meant.
acronymStudy.distinction: USB 3.1 Gen 1 is 5 Gb/s; USB 3.1 Gen 2 is 10 Gb/s.

acronymStudy.meaning: Converts between parallel data and asynchronous serial communication.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Universal serial data is Received and Transmitted Asynchronously.
acronymStudy.distinction: UART logic levels differ from RS-232 electrical levels.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects integrated circuits using a shared clocked two-wire interface.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Integrated Circuits Communicate on two shared signal lines.
acronymStudy.distinction: Voltage levels, addressing, pull-ups, and bus length matter.

sources.label: NXP I2C-bus specification and user manual

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects controllers and peripherals using synchronous serial signaling.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Serial Peripherals Interact through clocked wires.
acronymStudy.distinction: SPI conventions and device command protocols vary by implementation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides configurable digital input and output signals.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: General Purpose pins can take Input or send Output.
acronymStudy.distinction: Pin voltage and current limits must match the attached circuit.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names an industry alliance and interface specification family for embedded and mobile systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mobile components Interact through Processor Interfaces.
acronymStudy.distinction: MIPI is a family of specifications, not one universal connector.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects processors and displays through a MIPI display interface family.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Display data goes Serially through an Interface.
acronymStudy.distinction: DSI versions and physical-layer requirements must match the system.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects internal displays using an embedded DisplayPort interface.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: embedded Display Port stays inside the laptop.
acronymStudy.distinction: An internal eDP connector is not a general external DisplayPort receptacle.

sources.label: Samsung LCD backlighting and OLED pixels

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries signals using a low-voltage difference between paired conductors.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Low Voltage Difference carries the Signal.
acronymStudy.distinction: LVDS is an electrical signaling method, not one universal display protocol.

sources.label: Samsung LCD backlighting and OLED pixels

acronymStudy.meaning: Converts analog measurements into digital values.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Analog Data becomes Computer-readable as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Resolution, sampling rate, and signal conditioning affect measurement quality.

acronymStudy.meaning: Converts digital values into analog signals.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Digital data becomes an Analog waveform.
acronymStudy.distinction: This DAC differs from discretionary access control in security.

acronymStudy.meaning: Packages an integrated circuit using an array of solder-ball connections.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Balls form a Grid Under the chip as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: BGA attachment usually requires specialized equipment for rework.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Compute work is Unified on a Device Architecture.
acronymStudy.distinction: CUDA software and hardware compatibility depends on supported NVIDIA platforms.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides AMD's GPU computing software platform.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Radeon Opens Compute workflows.
acronymStudy.distinction: ROCm support depends on the specific GPU, OS, and software release.

acronymStudy.meaning: Accelerates tensor computations in Google's processor family.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Tensor operations get a specialized Processing Unit.
acronymStudy.distinction: TPU is a specific accelerator family rather than a generic label for all AI chips.

acronymStudy.meaning: Measures a rate of floating-point computation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Floating-point jobs Per Second count compute throughput.
acronymStudy.distinction: Precision, operation counting, and workload conditions must be specified.

acronymStudy.meaning: Expresses a rate of a trillion counted operations per second.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Tera = trillion Operations Per Second.
acronymStudy.distinction: Precision, sparsity, and counting conventions affect comparisons.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a commonly used 32-bit floating-point representation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Floating Point gets thirty-two bits.
acronymStudy.distinction: Numeric range and precision differ from lower-bit formats.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a 16-bit floating-point representation used in supported computation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Floating Point uses half as many bits as FP32.
acronymStudy.distinction: Reduced storage does not make all numerical behavior equivalent to FP32.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a 16-bit floating-point format with an exponent range like FP32.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Brain Float keeps a Broad exponent range as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: BF16 and IEEE FP16 have different exponent and precision layouts.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents integer values using eight bits in supported computation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Integer values fit Into eight bits.
acronymStudy.distinction: Quantized models also need scale, zero-point, or related interpretation rules.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents integer values using four bits in supported formats.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Integer values fit Into four bits.
acronymStudy.distinction: A four-bit model artifact can require additional metadata and runtime memory.

acronymStudy.meaning: Presents an immersive computer-generated environment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual surroundings Replace the visible world as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Headset resolution alone does not determine comfort or usability.

sources.label: Samsung LCD backlighting and OLED pixels

acronymStudy.meaning: Overlays digital information on a view of the physical environment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Augment Reality with extra digital information.
acronymStudy.distinction: Registration, latency, and context affect practical usefulness.

sources.label: Samsung LCD backlighting and OLED pixels

acronymStudy.meaning: Acts as an umbrella term for immersive and augmented experience technologies.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: eXtended Reality spans several experiences.
acronymStudy.distinction: XR is a category label, not a single display standard.

sources.label: Samsung LCD backlighting and OLED pixels

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects physical devices and embedded systems to networks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Things join the Internet.
acronymStudy.distinction: Connected devices need inventory, lifecycle support, and access controls.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects medical devices and related systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Medical Things join the network.
acronymStudy.distinction: Safety, privacy, clinical operations, and support constraints need coordinated planning.

acronymStudy.meaning: Monitors and controls industrial processes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Industrial processes have Control Systems.
acronymStudy.distinction: Safety and availability constraints can change patching and assessment approaches.

acronymStudy.meaning: Supervises industrial processes and acquires operational data.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Supervise, Control, and Acquire Data.
acronymStudy.distinction: SCADA systems can span distributed sites and specialized protocols.

acronymStudy.meaning: Executes control logic for industrial equipment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Programmable Logic Controls the machine.
acronymStudy.distinction: Unauthorized changes can affect physical operations and safety.

acronymStudy.meaning: Monitors or changes physical processes and equipment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Operational Technology touches physical Operations.
acronymStudy.distinction: OT security must account for safety and operational constraints.

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses substantial computing resources for demanding workloads.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: High Performance requires Coordinated computing.
acronymStudy.distinction: Cluster scale alone does not guarantee an application can use the resources efficiently.

acronymStudy.meaning: Routes within an autonomous system using link-state information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Open the map and choose the Shortest Path First.
acronymStudy.distinction: OSPF is an interior gateway protocol, unlike interdomain BGP.

acronymStudy.meaning: Exchanges routing information using a distance-vector approach.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Routing Information counts hops on the Path as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Classic RIP metrics and convergence limits constrain suitability.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides interior routing using a distance-vector-based design and DUAL.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Enhanced Interior routes are Guided by a Protocol.
acronymStudy.distinction: Protocol support and configuration compatibility need checking across platforms.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides gateway redundancy through an active and standby arrangement.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: A Hot Standby Router waits to take over.
acronymStudy.distinction: Gateway redundancy does not replace upstream connectivity redundancy.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a virtual default-router function with redundant participants.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual Routers Remain reachable through a Protocol.
acronymStudy.distinction: Timers, priority, and network design affect failover behavior.

acronymStudy.meaning: Combines gateway redundancy with distribution across forwarding devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Gateways Load Balance while Protecting access as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: GLBP support is platform-dependent.

acronymStudy.meaning: Forwards traffic using labels within a network.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Multiple Protocols ride Label-Switched paths.
acronymStudy.distinction: Private MPLS connectivity does not inherently encrypt payloads.

acronymStudy.meaning: Tunnels layer-2 sessions over packet networks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Layer Two travels through a Tunnel.
acronymStudy.distinction: L2TP alone does not provide encryption; it is often paired with IPsec.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 1701; IPsec-protected deployments also use IPsec/IKE transport

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a legacy remote-access tunneling protocol.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Point-to-Point traffic takes a legacy Tunnel.
acronymStudy.distinction: PPTP-based VPN security is obsolete; use supported modern alternatives.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a secure multiplexed transport over UDP.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Quick connections remember QUIC's purpose.
acronymStudy.distinction: QUIC is the protocol name; the historical Quick UDP Internet Connections phrase is not its current formal expansion.

acronymStudy.meaning: Authenticates DNS data using a chain of digital signatures.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS gets Security signatures as Extensions.
acronymStudy.distinction: DNSSEC validates data authenticity and integrity; it does not encrypt DNS queries.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries DNS queries and responses over HTTPS.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS rides over the HTTPS road.
acronymStudy.distinction: Encrypted transport does not by itself validate DNSSEC signatures or make a resolver trustworthy.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 443 commonly; HTTP/3-based deployments can use UDP 443

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries DNS queries and responses over TLS transport.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS rides over a TLS tunnel.
acronymStudy.distinction: DoT and DoH use different transport arrangements.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 853 by default

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines HTTP message syntax and connection behavior for version 1.1.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: One-point-one is the familiar text-message HTTP generation.
acronymStudy.distinction: HTTP/1.1 can be used with or without TLS depending on the connection scheme.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 80 commonly; HTTPS commonly uses TCP 443

acronymStudy.meaning: Multiplexes HTTP streams over a binary framing layer.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Two lets several streams share one connection.
acronymStudy.distinction: HTTP/2's common TCP transport still has transport-level head-of-line blocking.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 443 commonly for HTTPS

acronymStudy.meaning: Maps HTTP semantics onto QUIC.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Three takes HTTP onto the QUIC road.
acronymStudy.distinction: HTTP/3 is not HTTP/2 running over ordinary TCP.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 443 commonly for HTTPS over QUIC

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a TLS protocol version still supported in many environments.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Transport security generation one-point-two needs careful configuration.
acronymStudy.distinction: Algorithm choices and configuration matter; support alone is not proof of secure operation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Modernizes TLS handshakes and removes many legacy options.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: One-point-three trims old handshake baggage.
acronymStudy.distinction: Optional early data has replay considerations that applications must address.

acronymStudy.meaning: Adds an authentication extension to SMTP.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SMTP asks who is Authorized to submit mail.
acronymStudy.distinction: Authentication should use an appropriately protected connection and supported mechanisms.

acronymStudy.meaning: Describes content types and encodings for Internet messages.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mail Includes Many Encodings as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: MIME representation does not itself encrypt or authenticate a message.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a unit of information exchanged at a particular protocol layer.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Protocol rules wrap Data into a Unit.
acronymStudy.distinction: The unit's name and boundaries depend on the protocol layer.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names information supplied by one layer to the service of another.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Service receives Data before its own wrapping.
acronymStudy.distinction: An SDU at one interface can be carried inside another layer's PDU.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides the upper portion of the IEEE 802 data-link architecture.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Logical Links have a Control layer above media access.
acronymStudy.distinction: LLC and MAC describe different data-link sublayers.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries a frame integrity-check value used to detect transmission errors.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Frame arrives; Check its Sequence value.
acronymStudy.distinction: An FCS detects certain errors but is not cryptographic authentication.

acronymStudy.meaning: Computes an error-detection value using polynomial arithmetic.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Cycle through bits to Check for corruption.
acronymStudy.distinction: A CRC is not designed to resist intentional message tampering.

acronymStudy.meaning: Measures digital-link error behavior with a test pattern.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Bits are Exercised to Reveal Transmission errors.
acronymStudy.distinction: This BERT differs from the transformer model name used in machine learning.

acronymStudy.meaning: Expresses erroneous received bits relative to the evaluated bit population.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Bad bits divided by Evaluated bits gives the Ratio.
acronymStudy.distinction: State the test conditions and observation interval when comparing BER.

acronymStudy.meaning: Measures elapsed time for a request or packet exchange and its return.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Travel there and Return to Time the Trip.
acronymStudy.distinction: RTT includes more than physical propagation delay.

acronymStudy.meaning: Limits TCP payload size advertised for a connection direction.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Maximum Segment carries TCP data without its headers.
acronymStudy.distinction: MSS is different from a link's MTU.

acronymStudy.meaning: Limits IPv4 packet forwarding and also names DNS cache lifetime fields.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Traffic has a Travel Limit; cached records have a Time Limit.
acronymStudy.distinction: IPv4 TTL decreases at routers; DNS TTL represents seconds of cache lifetime.

acronymStudy.meaning: Marks an IP packet for differentiated traffic treatment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Different Services get a Code Point on the packet.
acronymStudy.distinction: A marking requests policy treatment; it does not guarantee bandwidth.

acronymStudy.meaning: Signals congestion using supported packet markings instead of only loss.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Explicitly Communicate Network congestion.
acronymStudy.distinction: Endpoints and network devices need compatible ECN behavior.

acronymStudy.meaning: Signals congestion by probabilistically dropping or marking packets before a queue fills.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Random Early action Detects a growing queue.
acronymStudy.distinction: RED is queue management, not an intrusion-detection technique.

acronymStudy.meaning: Applies differentiated early congestion signaling based on traffic treatment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Weighted traffic classes get RED behavior.
acronymStudy.distinction: Queue thresholds and classification policy affect the result.

acronymStudy.meaning: Centrally coordinates supported wireless access-point functions.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Wireless LANs have a Controller for their APs.
acronymStudy.distinction: Control-plane and data-forwarding arrangements vary by platform.

acronymStudy.expansion: Control and Provisioning of Wireless Access Points
acronymStudy.meaning: Defines control and related communication between wireless controllers and access points.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Control And Provision Wireless APs.
acronymStudy.distinction: CAPWAP is a protocol family, not the same thing as an SSID.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 5246 control and UDP 5247 data commonly

acronymStudy.meaning: Coordinates radio parameters such as channels and transmit power.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Radio Resources get a Manager.
acronymStudy.distinction: Automatic decisions still depend on site conditions and configuration.

acronymStudy.meaning: Changes radio channel use to avoid protected radar activity where required.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Dynamically Find a different Spectrum channel.
acronymStudy.distinction: DFS requirements depend on channel, region, and device class.

acronymStudy.meaning: Adjusts radio transmit power for operating requirements and link conditions.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Transmit Power is Controlled rather than always maximized.
acronymStudy.distinction: Higher transmit power does not necessarily improve a two-way wireless link.

acronymStudy.meaning: Protects selected wireless management frames against forgery and related attacks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Protect Management Frames, not just user data.
acronymStudy.distinction: PMF does not encrypt every management frame or eliminate all denial-of-service attacks.

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses DNSSEC-protected records to associate services with certificate information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS Authenticates Named Entities using secured records.
acronymStudy.distinction: DANE relies on appropriate DNSSEC validation and client support.

acronymStudy.meaning: Publishes which systems may send mail for a domain's envelope identity.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Sender Permission is Found in DNS as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: SPF does not directly authenticate the visible From header.

acronymStudy.meaning: Signs selected email content and headers on behalf of a domain.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Domain Keys Identify signed Mail.
acronymStudy.distinction: A valid signature does not establish that the message is harmless.

acronymStudy.expansion: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance
acronymStudy.meaning: Publishes handling and reporting policies using aligned SPF or DKIM results.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Domain Mail Aligns its identity, Reports, and Conforms.
acronymStudy.distinction: DMARC alignment relates authentication domains to the visible From domain.

acronymStudy.meaning: Transfers email between mail systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mail Travels through an Agent.
acronymStudy.distinction: An MTA has a different role from a user's mail client.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a user-facing application for composing and accessing email.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mail User opens an Application as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: A mail user agent need not directly deliver mail to the destination server.

acronymStudy.meaning: Delivers accepted email into its destination mailbox or local delivery system.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mail is Delivered by an Agent.
acronymStudy.distinction: Delivery to a mailbox does not mean the recipient read the message.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies mail-receiving hosts for a DNS domain.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mail eXchanges choose the receiving server.
acronymStudy.distinction: MX preference values express relative priority, not guaranteed availability.

acronymStudy.meaning: Maps a DNS name to another name, commonly for reverse-address lookup.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: A PoinTeR points back to a name.
acronymStudy.distinction: Reverse DNS does not prove ownership or trustworthiness of a service.

acronymStudy.meaning: Aliases one DNS name to another canonical name.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Canonical NAME is the destination behind an alias.
acronymStudy.distinction: A CNAME has coexistence constraints with other record types at the same owner name.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores text strings in DNS for application-defined uses.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: TeXT is placed into a DNS record.
acronymStudy.distinction: A TXT record's meaning is defined by the protocol using it.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores administrative and timing information at a DNS zone's origin.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Start Of Authority introduces a zone's administrative facts.
acronymStudy.distinction: A zone's SOA record is different from the list of its delegated name servers.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies authoritative DNS servers for a zone or delegation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Name Servers answer for the delegated namespace.
acronymStudy.distinction: An NS record names a server; address resolution can require additional records.

acronymStudy.meaning: Locates hosts and ports for specified DNS service names.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SeRVices publish where to connect.
acronymStudy.distinction: Priority, weight, port, and target have distinct meanings.

acronymStudy.meaning: Publishes which certificate authorities may issue certificates for a domain.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Certificate Authorities need Authorization.
acronymStudy.distinction: CAA constrains issuance policy; it does not revoke an already issued certificate.

acronymStudy.meaning: Transfers the complete contents of a DNS zone.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: All of the zone is transferred as the memory cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: AXFR is a DNS query-type mnemonic; restrict transfer access appropriately.

acronymStudy.meaning: Transfers DNS zone changes relative to a prior serial version.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Incremental changes make the Zone Transfer smaller.
acronymStudy.distinction: A server may need to fall back to a full transfer when suitable history is unavailable.

acronymStudy.meaning: Extends DNS messaging using mechanisms such as the OPT pseudo-record.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Extend DNS without replacing the whole naming system.
acronymStudy.distinction: Larger UDP responses can still encounter fragmentation or path issues.

acronymStudy.meaning: Resolves names on a local link using multicast queries.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Multicast lets nearby devices answer DNS questions.
acronymStudy.distinction: mDNS discovery is local-link behavior, not a replacement for enterprise DNS delegation.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 5353

acronymStudy.meaning: Advertises and discovers services using DNS record conventions.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS helps Services be Discovered.
acronymStudy.distinction: Service discovery does not itself authorize access to the discovered service.

acronymStudy.meaning: Groups networks under a common routing-policy administration.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Autonomous networks share one administrative System.
acronymStudy.distinction: An AS is a routing-policy concept, not a single router.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies an autonomous system in routing protocols and registries.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Autonomous Systems have Numbers.
acronymStudy.distinction: Public and private ASN use must follow the relevant allocation and routing rules.

acronymStudy.meaning: Exchanges routing information within an autonomous system.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Interior Gateways share Paths inside one AS.
acronymStudy.distinction: IGP is a protocol category rather than a single routing algorithm.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names both a category of interdomain routing protocols and an obsolete specific protocol.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Exterior Gateways exchange Paths between administrations.
acronymStudy.distinction: Modern BGP is an exterior gateway protocol; the original EGP protocol is historical.

acronymStudy.meaning: Exchanges link-state routing information between participating routers.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Intermediate Systems share their map with other Intermediate Systems.
acronymStudy.distinction: IS-IS uses different protocol machinery from OSPF despite both being link-state IGPs.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores topology information learned by a link-state routing process.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Link States become a DataBase of the network map.
acronymStudy.distinction: Database scope and synchronization rules depend on the routing protocol.

acronymStudy.meaning: Advertises topology or routing information in OSPF.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Link States are Advertised to build the map.
acronymStudy.distinction: OSPF LSA types carry different information and flooding scopes.

acronymStudy.meaning: Reduces adjacency and flooding complexity on supported OSPF multi-access networks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Designate one Router to coordinate the shared segment.
acronymStudy.distinction: This DR is not disaster recovery and is not necessarily the traffic's default gateway.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a standby designated-router role on eligible OSPF networks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Backup waits behind the Designated Router.
acronymStudy.distinction: DR and BDR election behavior depends on OSPF network type and priorities.

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses multiple routing next hops with equal routing cost.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Equal-Cost paths give Multiple choices.
acronymStudy.distinction: Per-flow hashing can keep a single flow on one path.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores routing information considered by a routing implementation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Routes are collected In a Base of information.
acronymStudy.distinction: The RIB and the forwarding table have different roles.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores forwarding information used to make packet-forwarding decisions.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Forwarding uses an Installed Base of next hops.
acronymStudy.distinction: FIB programming must reflect the intended control-plane routing decisions.

acronymStudy.meaning: Separates routing and forwarding contexts on supported network devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual Routes stay in separate Forwarding rooms.
acronymStudy.distinction: Separate routing tables do not by themselves provide encryption.

acronymStudy.meaning: Makes otherwise overlapping VPN routes distinguishable in supported routing systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Routes receive a Distinguishing label.
acronymStudy.distinction: A route distinguisher is different from a route target's import/export policy role.

acronymStudy.meaning: Labels routes for import and export policy in supported VPN routing systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Route Targets tell a VRF which routes to take.
acronymStudy.distinction: A route target is different from a route distinguisher.

acronymStudy.meaning: Encapsulates or decapsulates overlay traffic at a tunnel endpoint.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual Tunnels End at this Point.
acronymStudy.distinction: Overlay reachability still depends on a working underlay network.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries virtual layer-2 segments over a routed IP underlay.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual LANs eXtend across an IP network.
acronymStudy.distinction: VXLAN encapsulation is not encryption.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 4789 by default

acronymStudy.meaning: Distributes Ethernet VPN reachability using a control-plane model.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Ethernet networks gain a Virtual Private control plane.
acronymStudy.distinction: EVPN is commonly paired with VXLAN but is not the same protocol.

acronymStudy.meaning: Extends BGP to carry reachability for multiple address families.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Multiple Protocol families ride BGP.
acronymStudy.distinction: Address-family support and negotiated capabilities must match between peers.

acronymStudy.meaning: Rapidly checks forwarding-path connectivity between participating endpoints.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Both Forwarding Directions are Detected as alive.
acronymStudy.distinction: Aggressive timers can create false failures on overloaded or unstable systems.
acronymStudy.ports: UDP 3784 for single-hop control; UDP 3785 for supported echo traffic

acronymStudy.meaning: Integrates optical transceivers and fiber into a cable assembly.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Active electronics send light Over the Cable.
acronymStudy.distinction: Cable endpoints, reach, and supported port modes must match the system.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects compatible ports using a copper cable assembly with integrated ends.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Directly Attach the ports with Copper.
acronymStudy.distinction: This DAC is a cable type, not a digital-to-analog converter.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Exposes supported optical-module operating measurements.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Digital Diagnostics Monitor the transceiver.
acronymStudy.distinction: Available metrics and supported access depend on the module and host.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Reports optical transceiver conditions such as power and temperature.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Digital Optics Monitor their own health.
acronymStudy.distinction: DOM terminology overlaps with DDM; it does not define a new fiber category.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names an early standardized multimode optical-fiber category.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Multimode begins at category One.
acronymStudy.distinction: OM category describes fiber characteristics, not a universal link speed.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a multimode optical-fiber category with specified performance requirements.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Multimode steps to Two.
acronymStudy.distinction: Supported link reach depends on the transceiver and Ethernet standard.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names laser-optimized multimode optical fiber.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Multimode Three is designed for laser-driven links.
acronymStudy.distinction: Do not infer unlimited reach from a fiber-category label.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a higher-performance laser-optimized multimode optical-fiber category.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Multimode Four extends the multimode performance ladder.
acronymStudy.distinction: The optics and channel loss still constrain supported reach.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names wideband multimode optical fiber supporting specified wavelength ranges.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Multimode Five widens the wavelength window.
acronymStudy.distinction: OM5 does not make every legacy transceiver operate at a higher rate.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a standardized single-mode cabling category.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Single-mode One is the category cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: OS1 and OS2 have different specified attenuation characteristics.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a single-mode optical-fiber cabling category with lower specified attenuation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical Single-mode Two is suited to lower-loss channels.
acronymStudy.distinction: Link budget calculations still require actual channel and component losses.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries multiple optical channels using different wavelengths.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Wavelengths Divide one fiber into Multiple channels.
acronymStudy.distinction: Transmitters, receivers, and multiplexers must support the planned wavelengths.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Multiplexes optical channels with relatively wide wavelength spacing.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Coarse means wider spacing between Wavelengths.
acronymStudy.distinction: CWDM and DWDM use different channel plans and optical requirements.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Multiplexes closely spaced optical wavelengths.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Dense Wavelengths share the fiber.
acronymStudy.distinction: More channels require compatible optical design and power budgeting.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses reflected optical pulses to characterize fiber events and distance.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical pulse Time reveals Distance to a Reflection as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Interpret traces with awareness of launch conditions, dead zones, and connector reflections.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Organizes optical-fiber terminations and cross-connections.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optical fibers are Distributed on a Frame.
acronymStudy.distinction: Patch documentation and bend-radius practices remain essential.

sources.label: SNIA optical networking and storage dictionary

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides the network-side interface or timing role in traditional data circuits.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Data Circuit Equipment faces the communication line.
acronymStudy.distinction: DCE and DTE describe interface roles, not simply device size or connector gender.

acronymStudy.meaning: Acts as the terminal-side participant in traditional data communication interfaces.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Data Terminal Equipment is the endpoint needing the circuit.
acronymStudy.distinction: A device's DTE or DCE role depends on the interface arrangement.

acronymStudy.meaning: Performs digital-line interfacing functions in supported WAN equipment.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Data gets a Service Unit between router and circuit.
acronymStudy.distinction: DSU and CSU functions are often combined in a CSU/DSU device.

acronymStudy.meaning: Terminates and conditions supported digital carrier circuits.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Carrier Channels need a Service Unit.
acronymStudy.distinction: Legacy carrier interfaces differ from ordinary Ethernet access ports.

acronymStudy.meaning: Discovers directly connected Cisco-supported neighboring devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Cisco Devices Present themselves to neighbors.
acronymStudy.distinction: Discovery advertisements can reveal information and should follow network policy.

acronymStudy.meaning: Advertises device and port information to directly connected neighbors.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Link-Layer neighbors Discover each other's Ports.
acronymStudy.distinction: LLDP is link-local discovery, not an IP routing protocol.

acronymStudy.expansion: Link Layer Discovery Protocol Media Endpoint Discovery
acronymStudy.meaning: Extends LLDP for media endpoints such as IP phones.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Media Endpoints Discover voice-network information through LLDP.
acronymStudy.distinction: Endpoints and switches must support and permit the relevant policies.

acronymStudy.meaning: Distributes supported VLAN configuration information in Cisco environments.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: VLAN Tables are Propagated between switches.
acronymStudy.distinction: Incorrect domain, mode, version, or revision handling can disrupt VLAN configuration.

acronymStudy.meaning: Negotiates trunk behavior on supported Cisco switch ports.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Dynamically Talk about Trunking.
acronymStudy.distinction: Explicitly configuring intended port mode reduces unwanted trunk negotiation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Runs spanning-tree instances per VLAN on supported Cisco switches.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Per VLAN gets its own Spanning Tree.
acronymStudy.distinction: PVST+ and standards-based multiple spanning tree have different instance models.

acronymStudy.meaning: Maps VLANs to multiple spanning-tree instances.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Many VLANs Share Trees through Planned instances as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Region configuration must agree for switches to share an MST region.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries spanning-tree information between participating bridges.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Bridges exchange Protocol Data Units to avoid loops.
acronymStudy.distinction: BPDUs are control traffic, not ordinary user data frames.

acronymStudy.meaning: Mirrors selected switch traffic to a monitoring destination.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Switch Ports send copies to an Analyzer.
acronymStudy.distinction: Mirrored traffic can exceed destination capacity and lose packets.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries mirrored switch traffic to a remote observation point using supported layer-2 mechanisms.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Remote SPAN sends copies farther across the switched network.
acronymStudy.distinction: RSPAN configuration and transport differ from routed ERSPAN sessions.

acronymStudy.meaning: Encapsulates mirrored traffic for transport to remote monitoring tools.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Encapsulate Remote SPAN copies for the network trip.
acronymStudy.distinction: Mirroring can expose sensitive traffic; scope and secure monitoring access.

acronymStudy.meaning: Manages IPv4 multicast group membership between hosts and local routers.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Internet hosts tell the router which Groups they join.
acronymStudy.distinction: IGMP membership signaling is different from multicast routing between routers.

acronymStudy.meaning: Reports IPv6 multicast listener membership.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Multicast Listeners are Discovered on the IPv6 link.
acronymStudy.distinction: MLD is the IPv6 membership counterpart to IPv4 IGMP behavior.

acronymStudy.meaning: Builds multicast distribution using underlying unicast routing information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Multicast is Independent of a particular unicast routing Protocol.
acronymStudy.distinction: This PIM differs from privileged identity management.

acronymStudy.meaning: Delivers multicast identified by both a source and a group.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Specify the Source and the Multicast group.
acronymStudy.distinction: SSM differs from any-source multicast membership and rendezvous behavior.

acronymStudy.meaning: Discovers supported local-network services through discovery messages.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Simple Services announce how to be Discovered.
acronymStudy.distinction: Service discovery can reveal devices and should be scoped to trusted networks.

acronymStudy.meaning: Supports discovery and control of compatible network devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Plug in and Play with Universal device discovery.
acronymStudy.distinction: Automatic gateway mappings can expose services if enabled without appropriate controls.

acronymStudy.expansion: Network Address Translation from IPv6 to IPv4
acronymStudy.meaning: Translates traffic between supported IPv6 clients and IPv4 services.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Six-to-four addresses are Translated at the gateway.
acronymStudy.distinction: NAT64 behavior differs from an IPv6 tunnel carrying unchanged IPv4 packets.

acronymStudy.meaning: Synthesizes IPv6 address answers from IPv4 records for supported translation workflows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DNS builds a Six-format answer from a Four-format address as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: DNS64 commonly works with NAT64 and needs consideration of DNSSEC validation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a historical mechanism for carrying IPv6 traffic across IPv4 infrastructure.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Six travels over Four through an automatic tunnel.
acronymStudy.distinction: 6to4 is a protocol designation, not a word acronym; relay-dependent deployments are deprecated.

acronymStudy.expansion: Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode
acronymStudy.meaning: Combines AES encryption with authenticated-encryption processing in GCM.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: AES encrypts while GCM guards the message.
acronymStudy.distinction: Nonce reuse with the same key can critically undermine GCM security.

acronymStudy.expansion: Advanced Encryption Standard in Cipher Block Chaining mode
acronymStudy.meaning: Encrypts AES blocks using a chaining construction.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Each Cipher Block Chains to the prior block.
acronymStudy.distinction: CBC encryption alone does not authenticate ciphertext.

acronymStudy.expansion: Advanced Encryption Standard in Counter mode
acronymStudy.meaning: Generates an AES-based keystream from counter inputs.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: AES encrypts CounTeRs to make a stream.
acronymStudy.distinction: Never reuse the same key and counter sequence for different plaintexts.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides authenticated encryption using counter-mode encryption and a polynomial authenticator.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Galois checks integrity while the Counter encrypts.
acronymStudy.distinction: Key, nonce, and authentication-tag handling are all security-critical.

acronymStudy.meaning: Combines each plaintext block with prior ciphertext before block encryption.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Cipher Blocks form a Chain.
acronymStudy.distinction: CBC requires appropriate IV handling and a separate authentication strategy.

acronymStudy.meaning: Builds a stream-like encryption construction by encrypting counter blocks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: CounTeRs produce a changing keystream.
acronymStudy.distinction: Counter-mode encryption alone does not detect intentional modification.

acronymStudy.meaning: Encrypts each block independently with the same block-cipher key.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Equal plaintext Blocks get Equal ciphertext as the warning cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: ECB reveals repeated-block patterns and is unsuitable for general message encryption.

acronymStudy.meaning: Protects encrypted content and authenticates additional unencrypted context.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Authenticate Encryption And the extra Data.
acronymStudy.distinction: Associated data is authenticated but is not encrypted by that role.

acronymStudy.meaning: Supplies integrity-protected context to supported authenticated-encryption schemes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Additional Data is Authenticated alongside the ciphertext.
acronymStudy.distinction: AAD can be visible to observers even when its integrity is protected.

acronymStudy.meaning: Initializes a supported cryptographic mode's state or processing.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Initialize the cipher with a starting Vector.
acronymStudy.distinction: Uniqueness and unpredictability requirements depend on the mode.

acronymStudy.meaning: Derives key material from input secrets and context.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Keys are Derived through a Function.
acronymStudy.distinction: A KDF is not interchangeable with arbitrary truncation of an unkeyed hash.

acronymStudy.meaning: Derives key material from a password with a salt and iteration count.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Passwords Become Keys through repeated Derivation.
acronymStudy.distinction: Choose work factors deliberately; PBKDF2 is not inherently a memory-hard construction.

acronymStudy.meaning: Derives keys using extraction and expansion based on HMAC.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: HMAC first extracts, then expands Key material.
acronymStudy.distinction: HKDF is not designed to slow password guessing like a password-hardening function.

acronymStudy.meaning: Creates RSA signatures using probabilistic encoding.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: RSA signs with Probabilistic Salted Structure as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: RSA-PSS is a signature scheme, not an encryption scheme.

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses RSA encryption with OAEP encoding.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: RSA encryption gets an Asymmetric Padding envelope.
acronymStudy.distinction: OAEP is for encryption and differs from PSS signature encoding.

acronymStudy.meaning: Encodes messages for supported asymmetric encryption schemes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Optimal Asymmetric Encryption needs Padding.
acronymStudy.distinction: Use the defined scheme and parameter rules rather than inventing padding.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a probabilistic encoding used with RSA signatures.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Probabilistic signatures use a Salted Scheme as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Signature verification must use compatible algorithm parameters.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a family of specifications for public-key cryptographic formats and interfaces.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Public Keys get Cryptography Standards.
acronymStudy.distinction: Each numbered PKCS specification has a distinct purpose.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a cryptographic-token interface used by software and secure devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Eleven opens an Interface to cryptographic tokens as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Interface compatibility does not establish a device's security certification or policy.

acronymStudy.meaning: Packages private keys, certificates, and related information in a defined format.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Twelve packs the key-and-certificate Travel bag as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: A private-key package needs strong protection and controlled handling.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a historical secure-mail framework whose textual encoding conventions are widely reused.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Privacy-Enhanced Mail left its familiar BEGIN and END wrappers.
acronymStudy.distinction: A PEM wrapper describes an encoding label, not whether the enclosed private key is encrypted.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a canonical binary encoding for ASN.1 data.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Distinguished rules choose one precise Encoding.
acronymStudy.distinction: DER is an encoding, not an encryption algorithm.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines data structures independently of their transfer encoding.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Abstract structures get Syntax Notation number One.
acronymStudy.distinction: ASN.1 describes structure; BER and DER define encoding rules.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies objects or algorithm names using a hierarchical identifier namespace.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Objects have IDs along a dotted tree.
acronymStudy.distinction: An OID's meaning depends on its assigned namespace and specification.

acronymStudy.meaning: Lists alternative identities in a certificate extension.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Subject names get Alternatives on the certificate.
acronymStudy.distinction: This SAN is a certificate field, not a storage area network.

acronymStudy.meaning: Constrains a certificate's permitted application purposes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Extend the certificate's Key-Usage purpose list.
acronymStudy.distinction: EKU and the Key Usage extension express different constraints.

acronymStudy.meaning: Constrains cryptographic uses of a certificate's key.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: The Key has a Usage permission list.
acronymStudy.distinction: A valid chain alone does not mean the key is authorized for every purpose.

acronymStudy.meaning: Helps identify the public key associated with a certificate subject.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Subject's Key gets an Identifier.
acronymStudy.distinction: An SKI aids identification and is not by itself a trust decision.

acronymStudy.meaning: Helps identify the issuing authority's signing key.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Authority's Key gets an Identifier.
acronymStudy.distinction: An AKI is not a replacement for certificate-path validation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Authenticates both peers using TLS mechanisms, commonly certificates.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Mutual means both sides prove who they are.
acronymStudy.distinction: Application authorization is still required after successful mutual authentication.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names an account using a user-and-suffix style identity in supported directories.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: User Principal has a Name that often resembles email.
acronymStudy.distinction: A UPN can differ from the user's email address.

acronymStudy.meaning: Stores local Windows account security information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Security Accounts have a local Manager.
acronymStudy.distinction: SAM local accounts differ from Active Directory domain accounts.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies Windows security principals and related security entities.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Security principals have an ID.
acronymStudy.distinction: Renaming an account does not necessarily change its SID.

acronymStudy.meaning: Forms the domain-relative or authority-relative portion of supported SIDs.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Relative ID is the unique tail within its authority.
acronymStudy.distinction: A RID alone is not a globally complete Windows account identifier.

acronymStudy.meaning: Lists permission entries controlling access to a Windows securable object.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Discretionary Access is Controlled by a List.
acronymStudy.distinction: A null DACL and an empty DACL have different access implications.

acronymStudy.meaning: Contains supported auditing and related system security entries.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: System auditing has its own Access Control List.
acronymStudy.distinction: An audit SACL does not serve the same permission-granting role as a DACL.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents an individual entry in an access-control list.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: An Access decision reads each Control Entry.
acronymStudy.distinction: Entry types, ordering, inheritance, and evaluation semantics matter.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents Windows security descriptors in a defined string notation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Security Descriptors have a Definition Language.
acronymStudy.distinction: Read owner, group, permissions, and audit components in their proper context.

acronymStudy.meaning: Identifies a service instance for supported Kerberos authentication workflows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Service Principal needs a unique Name.
acronymStudy.distinction: Duplicate or incorrect SPNs can break authentication or create security problems.

acronymStudy.meaning: Obtains service tickets in a Kerberos authentication flow.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: A Ticket Grants access to more Tickets.
acronymStudy.distinction: A TGT is a sensitive credential and should not be exposed in logs.

acronymStudy.meaning: Issues Kerberos service tickets after appropriate authentication.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Ticket Granting is a Service of the KDC.
acronymStudy.distinction: A TGS is a service role; a service ticket is the issued credential.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides Kerberos authentication and ticket services.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Keys and tickets are Distributed from a Center.
acronymStudy.distinction: KDC availability, key protection, and correct time support reliable authentication.

acronymStudy.meaning: Carries Windows authorization information in supported Kerberos tickets.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Privileges and Attributes ride in a Certificate-like data structure.
acronymStudy.distinction: A Kerberos PAC differs from a proxy auto-configuration file.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a Windows domain service-account type with managed credentials and supported multi-host use.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Group services get a Managed Service Account.
acronymStudy.distinction: Authorized hosts and service compatibility must be configured deliberately.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a managed Windows service account for a single supported computer.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Standalone means one host gets the Managed Service Account.
acronymStudy.distinction: sMSA deployment differs from the multi-host gMSA model.

acronymStudy.meaning: Manages supported local administrator passwords with controlled retrieval.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Local Admin Passwords get a Solution for rotation.
acronymStudy.distinction: Legacy Microsoft LAPS and Windows LAPS have different capabilities and deployment requirements.

acronymStudy.meaning: Supports Microsoft Entra single sign-on and token acquisition on supported devices.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Primary token helps Refresh sign-in Tokens.
acronymStudy.distinction: A PRT is sensitive authentication material, not an ordinary application setting.

acronymStudy.meaning: Standardizes identity-resource provisioning and management across systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Systems Coordinate Identity Management as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: SCIM provisioning is different from authenticating a user with SAML or OIDC.

acronymStudy.meaning: Responds to supported identity and policy events during application access.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Continuously Assess whether access remains Eligible as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: CAE behavior depends on compatible clients, services, events, and policies.

acronymStudy.meaning: Applies identity access decisions using signals, policy, and supported controls.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Conditions Affect whether access is granted.
acronymStudy.distinction: This CA is an access-policy capability, not a certificate authority.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names an alliance and authentication standards ecosystem.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Fast Identity moves Online using strong authenticators.
acronymStudy.distinction: FIDO is broader than the FIDO2 standards combination.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines an earlier FIDO public-key second-factor authentication approach.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: A Universal second Factor supports stronger sign-in.
acronymStudy.distinction: U2F and modern WebAuthn/CTAP deployments have different capability models.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a FIDO authentication framework for supported passwordless use cases.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Universal Authentication follows a Framework.
acronymStudy.distinction: UAF is distinct from FIDO U2F and FIDO2.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a web API for public-key credential registration and authentication.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Web Authentication shortens to WebAuthn.
acronymStudy.distinction: WebAuthn is a specification name; relying-party scope and origin validation are fundamental.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects clients with external authenticators in supported FIDO flows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Client Talks to the Authenticator through a Protocol.
acronymStudy.distinction: CTAP and the browser's WebAuthn API operate at different interfaces.

acronymStudy.meaning: Detects relevant changes to monitored files or other configured objects.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: File Integrity changes are Monitored.
acronymStudy.distinction: A detected change needs context to distinguish authorized work from compromise.

acronymStudy.meaning: Blocks selected suspicious activity on an individual host.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Host Intrusions are Prevented at the System.
acronymStudy.distinction: Prevention policies can interfere with legitimate activity if configured poorly.

acronymStudy.meaning: Inspects and can block selected suspicious network traffic.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Network Intrusions are Prevented inline.
acronymStudy.distinction: Encrypted traffic and sensor placement affect inspection coverage.

acronymStudy.meaning: Uses network telemetry to detect, investigate, and respond to threats.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Network events drive Detection and Response.
acronymStudy.distinction: Network visibility complements endpoint and identity telemetry.

acronymStudy.meaning: Analyzes user and entity behavior for security-relevant anomalies.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Users and Entities have Behaviors to Analyze.
acronymStudy.distinction: An unusual pattern is a lead for investigation, not proof of malicious intent.

acronymStudy.meaning: Analyzes user activity for meaningful behavioral patterns or anomalies.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: User Behavior gets Analyzed over time.
acronymStudy.distinction: UBA focuses on users; UEBA also includes other entity types.

acronymStudy.meaning: Organizes threat-intelligence collection, analysis, and sharing.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Threat Intelligence has a Platform for coordination.
acronymStudy.distinction: A platform does not guarantee the intelligence is timely or relevant.

acronymStudy.meaning: Applies context and analysis to information about cyber threats.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Cyber Threat facts become useful Intelligence.
acronymStudy.distinction: Raw indicators and finished intelligence have different levels of interpretation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents cyber-threat intelligence using defined structured objects and relationships.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Structured Threat Information is eXpressed consistently.
acronymStudy.distinction: STIX is a representation standard, not a transport protocol.

acronymStudy.expansion: Trusted Automated Exchange of Intelligence Information
acronymStudy.meaning: Exchanges supported cyber-threat intelligence through standardized services.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Threat intelligence is Automatically eXchanged through an Interface as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: TAXII transport does not establish the truth of the intelligence being shared.

acronymStudy.expansion: Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge
acronymStudy.meaning: Organizes observed adversary behaviors and their relationships.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Adversaries use Tactics and Techniques; defenders collect Common Knowledge.
acronymStudy.distinction: ATT&CK technique coverage is not a complete measurement of security effectiveness.

acronymStudy.meaning: Classifies types of software and hardware weaknesses.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Weaknesses are Enumerated by type.
acronymStudy.distinction: CWE classifies weakness types; CVE identifies particular disclosed vulnerabilities.

acronymStudy.expansion: Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification
acronymStudy.meaning: Describes reusable patterns of attack behavior.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Attack Patterns are Enumerated and Classified.
acronymStudy.distinction: An attack pattern differs from a specific vulnerability identifier.

sources.label: MITRE Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification

acronymStudy.meaning: Names classes of hardware, operating systems, and applications in a structured format.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Platforms have Enumerated names.
acronymStudy.distinction: Product matching still needs accurate version and configuration information.

acronymStudy.meaning: Combines specifications for automated security configuration and vulnerability information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Security Content is Automated through Protocol specifications.
acronymStudy.distinction: SCAP is a suite of standards, not one vulnerability scanner.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents supported machine-state checks in a standardized language.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Open Vulnerability checks use an Assessment Language.
acronymStudy.distinction: OVAL definitions and collected state need appropriate interpretation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Describes security checklists, benchmarks, and evaluation results.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: eXtensible Checklists Capture Configuration Details in a Format as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: XCCDF organizes checklist content rather than performing every underlying check itself.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a structured format for vulnerability advisories.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Vulnerability Reports follow a Framework.
acronymStudy.distinction: CVRF is a predecessor to newer CSAF advisory-format work.

acronymStudy.meaning: Represents machine-readable security advisories using a defined framework.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Security Advisories have a Format as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Advisory data must still be matched to the organization's actual assets.

acronymStudy.meaning: Communicates whether a known vulnerability affects a particular product context.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Vulnerability Exploitability gets eXplained for a product.
acronymStudy.distinction: A not-affected statement needs scope, justification, and a trustworthy issuer.

acronymStudy.meaning: Defines a framework for improving software supply-chain integrity.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Software's supply chain needs Levels of assurance.
acronymStudy.distinction: A provenance record alone does not automatically satisfy every SLSA requirement.

acronymStudy.meaning: Groups cloud-delivered access-security capabilities.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Security Services sit at the Edge.
acronymStudy.distinction: SSE focuses on security services and is distinct from the broader SASE architecture.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides policy-based access to specific applications or resources.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Zero Trust grants Needed Application access as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: ZTNA is an access approach, not proof that every part of a system implements zero trust.

acronymStudy.meaning: Applies security policy to web traffic and access.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Secure Web traffic passes a Gateway.
acronymStudy.distinction: Inspection capabilities depend on deployment, encryption handling, and policy.

acronymStudy.meaning: Labels information-sharing permissions using a defined color-based convention.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Traffic Lights guide how far information may travel.
acronymStudy.distinction: TLP is a sharing protocol and is not a formal government classification scheme.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides unauthorized remote access through malicious software.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: A Remote attacker gains Access through a Trojan.
acronymStudy.distinction: Remote administration tools can also be legitimate; intent and authorization matter.

acronymStudy.meaning: Coordinates an adversary's instructions and communications with compromised systems.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Two Cs: Command and Control.
acronymStudy.distinction: C2 can use ordinary protocols, so a protocol name alone is not an attack verdict.

acronymStudy.meaning: Chains existing instruction sequences to alter program execution.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Return instructions link small code Pieces as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: ROP reuses existing code rather than requiring all payload instructions to be newly injected.

acronymStudy.meaning: Marks supported memory regions as non-executable to reduce exploitation paths.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Data pages should not Execute Programs as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: DEP reduces some exploit techniques but is not a complete exploit defense.

acronymStudy.meaning: Randomizes supported process memory layout locations.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Address Spaces Land in Random places as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Effectiveness depends on entropy, coverage, and interactions with other mitigations.

acronymStudy.meaning: Handles supported Windows exception-processing flows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Structured Exceptions have a Handler.
acronymStudy.distinction: SEH is a programming and OS mechanism, not inherently a security vulnerability.

acronymStudy.meaning: Protects supported Windows exception-handler chains against certain overwrite attacks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SEH Overwrites get Protection.
acronymStudy.distinction: SEHOP addresses a class of exploitation and does not replace other mitigations.

acronymStudy.expansion: Time of Check to Time of Use
acronymStudy.meaning: Describes a race when state changes between validation and later use.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: The Check happens now; the Use happens later.
acronymStudy.distinction: Performing a check is insufficient when the checked state can change before use.

acronymStudy.meaning: Exposes objects through identifiers without appropriate authorization checks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: An ID Opens a Resource without permission as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Hard-to-guess identifiers do not replace per-object authorization.

acronymStudy.meaning: Fails to enforce access rules on individual objects.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Broken Object Locks Allow unwanted access as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Authenticate the caller and separately authorize each object operation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Describes an attack involving unsafe processing of external XML entities.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: XML eXternal Entities can pull unwanted resources.
acronymStudy.distinction: Disable or constrain dangerous entity resolution according to parser and application requirements.

acronymStudy.meaning: Injects unintended template expressions into server-side rendering.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Server Templates Interpret hostile input as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Template escaping and safe handling depend on the template engine and context.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names a control-character sequence that can be abused in text-based protocol injection.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Carriage Returns, then the Line Feeds.
acronymStudy.distinction: CRLF is a character sequence; injection occurs when untrusted data changes protocol structure.

acronymStudy.meaning: Changes directory queries through unsafe handling of untrusted input.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: LDAP input Invades the filter structure.
acronymStudy.distinction: Escape or parameterize using the directory API's rules for the specific context.

acronymStudy.expansion: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege
acronymStudy.meaning: Categorizes threats using six classes of undesirable behavior.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Walk through each STRIDE category while reviewing a data flow.
acronymStudy.distinction: STRIDE categories guide analysis rather than proving that every threat has been found.

acronymStudy.expansion: Damage potential, Reproducibility, Exploitability, Affected users, and Discoverability
acronymStudy.meaning: Names a historical threat-rating model using five dimensions.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: DREAD asks about Damage, Repeatability, Ease, Audience, and Discovery as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: Scoring can be subjective; define the rating method and its limitations.

acronymStudy.expansion: Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis
acronymStudy.meaning: Structures risk-oriented threat modeling around business and technical context.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Process the Attack through Simulation and Threat Analysis.
acronymStudy.distinction: PASTA is a methodology, not a single automated attack tool.

acronymStudy.expansion: Operationally Critical Threat, Asset, and Vulnerability Evaluation
acronymStudy.meaning: Evaluates organizational information-security risks using operational context.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Operationally Critical Assets face Threats and Vulnerabilities to Evaluate.
acronymStudy.distinction: OCTAVE is a risk-evaluation approach rather than a vulnerability-scanning product.

acronymStudy.meaning: Structures quantitative analysis of information risk.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Factors are Analyzed to estimate Information Risk.
acronymStudy.distinction: Quantitative outputs still depend on evidence quality and assumptions.

acronymStudy.expansion: Visual, Agile, and Simple Threat modeling
acronymStudy.meaning: Names a threat-modeling approach designed for scalable organizational workflows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Visual diagrams support Agile, Simple Threat modeling.
acronymStudy.distinction: VAST is methodology terminology; suitability depends on the organization and implementation.

acronymStudy.meaning: Groups related Azure resources for management and lifecycle operations.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Related Resources go into a Group.
acronymStudy.distinction: A resource group is a management container, not an availability or network-isolation boundary.

sources.label: Azure Resource Manager scope and organization

acronymStudy.meaning: Organizes Azure subscriptions into a governance hierarchy.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Management Groups gather subscriptions above resource groups.
acronymStudy.distinction: Policy and access inheritance need deliberate scope design.

sources.label: Azure Resource Manager scope and organization

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects to a supported service using a private IP endpoint in an Azure virtual network.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Private access enters through an Endpoint in the VNet.
acronymStudy.distinction: A private endpoint does not automatically disable all public access to the service.

acronymStudy.meaning: Publishes a supported customer service for consumption through Azure Private Link.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Private Link has a Service provider side.
acronymStudy.distinction: A Private Link Service and a consumer's private endpoint have different roles.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names the former branding for Microsoft Entra ID.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Azure AD changed its name to Entra ID.
acronymStudy.distinction: AAD is a legacy product name; Microsoft Entra ID is distinct from on-premises AD DS.

acronymStudy.meaning: Names the former branding for Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Azure AD's Domain Services now wear the Entra name.
acronymStudy.distinction: Managed domain services differ from Microsoft Entra ID's cloud identity platform.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides an Azure-supported workload identity with credentials managed by the platform.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Managed Identity moves credential maintenance to the platform.
acronymStudy.distinction: The identity still needs explicit authorization to its target resources.

acronymStudy.meaning: Creates a managed identity as a separately managed Azure resource.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: User Assigns one Managed Identity to supported resources.
acronymStudy.distinction: Its lifecycle is independent of an individual resource using it.

acronymStudy.meaning: Creates a managed identity tied to a supported Azure resource's lifecycle.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: System Assigns the identity to this resource's life.
acronymStudy.distinction: Deleting the resource also removes its associated system-assigned identity.

acronymStudy.meaning: Manages groups of Azure virtual machines using supported orchestration modes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Virtual Machines Scale as a Set.
acronymStudy.distinction: Scaling behavior depends on orchestration, capacity rules, and application design.

sources.label: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview

acronymStudy.meaning: Distributes supported transport-layer traffic across healthy backend resources.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Load is Balanced among the Azure backends.
acronymStudy.distinction: Azure Load Balancer is different from an HTTP-aware application gateway.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a load-balancing frontend reachable through a private network address.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Internal clients reach the private Load Balancer.
acronymStudy.distinction: Internal addressing does not replace authentication or application authorization.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides Azure HTTP-aware application delivery and routing capabilities.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Application traffic passes through a Gateway.
acronymStudy.distinction: WAF capability depends on the selected product tier and configuration.

acronymStudy.meaning: Groups physically separate datacenter infrastructure within a supported Azure region.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Availability is separated into Zones within the region.
acronymStudy.distinction: Zone support and resilient deployment behavior vary by service and region.

sources.label: Azure availability options for virtual machines

acronymStudy.meaning: Distributes supported Azure virtual machines across platform fault and update domains.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Availability Set members avoid sharing every failure domain.
acronymStudy.distinction: An availability set is different from an availability zone deployment.

sources.label: Azure availability options for virtual machines

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides standardized, maintained infrastructure modules for supported Azure deployment tooling.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Azure has Verified Modules for repeatable infrastructure.
acronymStudy.distinction: Using a module does not remove responsibility for parameters, permissions, cost, or deployment review.

acronymStudy.meaning: Groups supported Azure Monitor resources for private-link access design.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Azure Monitor Private Links have a shared Scope.
acronymStudy.distinction: DNS, endpoint, ingestion, and query access settings all affect the final behavior.

acronymStudy.meaning: Collects supported monitoring data under Azure Monitor configuration.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Azure Monitor has an Agent on the machine.
acronymStudy.distinction: AMA collection depends on supported rules, associations, and platform configuration.

sources.label: Azure Monitor Agent and legacy-agent migration

acronymStudy.meaning: Names the legacy monitoring agent associated with older Log Analytics collection workflows.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Microsoft Monitoring had an older Agent before AMA.
acronymStudy.distinction: MMA is retired; plan supported Azure Monitor Agent migration rather than a new legacy deployment.

sources.label: Azure Monitor Agent and legacy-agent migration

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides connection information for supported Azure Monitor data collection and access scenarios.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Data Collection uses a configured Endpoint.
acronymStudy.distinction: This DCE is an Azure monitoring resource, not traditional data circuit-terminating equipment.

acronymStudy.expansion: Redundant Array of Independent Disks level 0
acronymStudy.meaning: Stripes data across multiple disks for supported performance or capacity goals.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Zero means zero redundant copies or parity.
acronymStudy.distinction: Failure of a member can make the striped data unavailable; RAID 0 is not fault tolerant.

acronymStudy.expansion: Redundant Array of Independent Disks level 1
acronymStudy.meaning: Mirrors data across supported member disks.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: One logical dataset has mirrored copies.
acronymStudy.distinction: Mirroring improves selected failure tolerance but is not an independent backup.

acronymStudy.expansion: Redundant Array of Independent Disks level 5
acronymStudy.meaning: Stripes data with distributed single-parity information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Five has one parity-equivalent disk of capacity as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: A conventional RAID 5 set tolerates one member-disk failure, not two simultaneous member failures.

acronymStudy.expansion: Redundant Array of Independent Disks level 6
acronymStudy.meaning: Stripes data with dual distributed parity information.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Six adds a second parity protection layer beyond five.
acronymStudy.distinction: Conventional RAID 6 tolerates two member-disk failures; rebuild time and other failures still matter.

acronymStudy.expansion: Redundant Array of Independent Disks level 10
acronymStudy.meaning: Stripes data across mirrored groups in a nested layout.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: One plus zero: mirror first, then stripe.
acronymStudy.distinction: Failure tolerance depends on which disks fail, not just the total failure count.

acronymStudy.meaning: Distributes redundancy across independent system nodes.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: RAID-like resilience moves from disks to Nodes.
acronymStudy.distinction: Node redundancy needs an appropriate data-placement and failure-domain design.

acronymStudy.meaning: Describes exposing or aggregating disks without a RAID redundancy scheme implied by the term.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Just a Bunch means no promised RAID protection.
acronymStudy.distinction: Some products use JBOD differently; inspect the controller's actual disk presentation mode.

acronymStudy.meaning: Connects a host to a peripheral or storage interconnect.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Host talks to the Bus through an Adapter.
acronymStudy.distinction: An HBA is not automatically a hardware RAID controller.

acronymStudy.meaning: Encapsulates Fibre Channel traffic over supported Ethernet fabrics.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Fibre Channel rides over Ethernet.
acronymStudy.distinction: FCoE requires compatible fabric behavior and is distinct from iSCSI over TCP/IP.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides network filesystem access through a defined protocol family.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Network Files are shared as a System.
acronymStudy.distinction: NFS versions have different state, authentication, and protocol capabilities.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 2049 commonly for NFSv4; older arrangements can use additional RPC services

acronymStudy.meaning: Names the legacy SMB file-sharing protocol generation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SMB One is the old sharing generation.
acronymStudy.distinction: SMBv1 is obsolete and should be removed where dependencies allow a supported migration.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 445 for direct-hosted SMB; older NetBIOS arrangements use additional ports

acronymStudy.meaning: Revises SMB file-sharing operations with a newer protocol design.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SMB Two replaces many older SMB One behaviors.
acronymStudy.distinction: Features differ across SMB 2.x dialects and implementations.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 445 commonly

acronymStudy.meaning: Adds modern SMB capabilities including supported encryption and availability features.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: SMB Three adds stronger sharing capabilities.
acronymStudy.distinction: Encryption and other features depend on negotiated dialect, configuration, and endpoint support.
acronymStudy.ports: TCP 445 commonly; supported alternate transports have their own requirements

acronymStudy.meaning: Names an SMB-related legacy file-sharing specification and terminology.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Common Internet Files are shared through an older System.
acronymStudy.distinction: CIFS terminology often refers to SMBv1-era behavior and should not describe every modern SMB feature.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides Ceph's distributed object-storage foundation.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: Reliable objects are Automatically Distributed by the Store as a cue.
acronymStudy.distinction: RADOS is the storage foundation beneath higher-level Ceph interfaces.

acronymStudy.meaning: Exposes block devices backed by Ceph RADOS storage.
acronymStudy.mnemonic: RADOS gives a virtual Block Device.
acronymStudy.distinction: Block-device features depend on client, cluster version, and image configuration.

acronymStudy.meaning: Provides a distributed filesystem backed by Ceph.
